title: AbbVie Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenue Rises 10% to $17.4 Billion and 2026 EPS Guidance Is Raised
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $3.82 topped estimates as Skyrizi and Rinvoq grew more than 22% each, prompting a guidance raise, a higher Skyrizi target and a 5.2% dividend increase.
body:
• AbbVie beat third-quarter estimates on both lines: adjusted EPS of $3.82 against the $3.74 Zacks consensus and management's own $3.73–$3.77 guidance, on revenue of $17.404 billion, up 10.3%.
  • Immunology drove the quarter: portfolio revenue rose 16.6% operationally to $9.165 billion, with Skyrizi up 22.9% to $5.776 billion and Rinvoq up 24.3% to $2.706 billion, swamping Humira's 30.6% decline to $683 million; neuroscience grew 19.5% to $3.389 billion.
  • AbbVie raised and narrowed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95–$13.99 from $13.76–$13.96, lifted its revenue outlook to about $67.8 billion, and raised Skyrizi's full-year target for a third time, to $21.8 billion.
  • The board increased the quarterly dividend 5.2% to $1.82 per share, beginning with the payment in February 2027, and AbbVie closed its acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics.

AbbVie delivered another beat-and-raise quarter on Friday, reporting third-quarter 2026 results in its official earnings release that topped Wall Street estimates and its own guidance, powered by its immunology blockbusters and a fast-growing neuroscience business. Adjusted earnings were $3.82 per diluted share, above the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.74 and management's guided range of $3.73 to $3.77, while GAAP diluted EPS was $2.37. Both EPS figures more than doubled from a year earlier, when a far larger acquired research and development charge weighed on results, and each absorbed an $0.11-per-share hit from acquired IPR&D and milestone expenses this quarter.

Skyrizi and Rinvoq carry the growth

Worldwide net revenues were $17.404 billion, up 10.3% on a reported basis and 10.5% operationally, ahead of the $17.37 billion consensus and the company's $17.2 billion guidance. Immunology remained the engine: portfolio revenues rose to $9.165 billion, with Skyrizi at $5.776 billion, up 22.9% and ahead of the $5.72 billion estimate, and Rinvoq at $2.706 billion, up 24.3%. Together the two drugs produced about $8.5 billion — nearly half of total revenue — and more than covered continued erosion of Humira, down 30.6% to $683 million as biosimilar competition bites.

Neuroscience was the standout secondary business, with revenues up 19.5% to $3.389 billion, ahead of the $3.29 billion consensus, led by Botox Therapeutic at $1.080 billion and Vraylar at $1.068 billion. Oncology revenue was nearly flat at about $1.696 billion. Profitability stayed high, with an adjusted operating margin of 48.7% and an adjusted gross margin of 85.1%, and profit growth was flattered by the comparison: acquired IPR&D and milestone expense fell to $216 million from $2.68 billion a year ago.

“AbbVie continues to deliver outstanding results, reflecting solid execution across our diverse portfolio.”

— Robert A. Michael, Chairman and CEO, AbbVie

Guidance up, dividend up

Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $13.95–$13.99 from $13.76–$13.96, a range that includes a $0.69-per-share adverse impact from acquired IPR&D and milestones incurred through the third quarter. On the earnings call, the company also lifted its full-year revenue outlook by $200 million to about $67.8 billion, raised Skyrizi's full-year sales target for the third time this year to $21.8 billion, and guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $18.4 billion with adjusted EPS of $3.83–$3.87 before any further IPR&D charges.

AbbVie also completed its acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics during the quarter, adding immunology pipeline assets including zumilokibart and APG273, and generated roughly $14 billion of free cash flow in the first nine months of the year. The board's 5.2% dividend increase, to $1.82 per share from $1.73, begins with the dividend payable February 16, 2027. Shares rose on Friday as analysts called the quarter another step in AbbVie's post-Humira transition.
